name: Apache Druid
tagline: Real-time analytics database for sub-second slice-and-dice over streaming event data.
description: Apache Druid is a distributed column store built for interactive analytics on event data. It ingests straight from Kafka or Kinesis so events are queryable within seconds, stores data in time-partitioned, bitmap-indexed segments on deep storage, and answers high-concurrency group-by and filter queries in sub-second time. Its multi-stage query engine added SQL-based batch ingestion and querying of data in deep storage. Druid is a strong fit for user-facing dashboards and operational analytics; it has many process types to operate and is less suited to ad-hoc warehouse-style joins.

pricing.notes: Free to self-host; Imply offers commercial distributions and the Imply Polaris cloud service.

scale.notes: Scales each service (brokers, historicals, ingestion) independently; segments live in S3/HDFS deep storage.

strengths: Exactly-once streaming ingestion from Kafka and Kinesis with seconds of latency
Sub-second queries at high concurrency for dashboards and APIs
Bitmap indexes and time partitioning make filters and group-bys fast
Rollup at ingest time cuts storage for high-cardinality events
Tiered storage and query-from-deep-storage for cheap historical data
weaknesses: Many node types (coordinator, overlord, broker, historical, middle manager) to operate
Joins are limited compared with a full SQL warehouse
Smaller community momentum than ClickHouse in recent years
notIdealFor: Ad-hoc complex joins across many tables
Small datasets where a single-node DB suffices
